$comment-versioning: this comment was Jeles's, copied verbatim with the rest of this release pipeline; corrected 2026-09-12 to this repository's own facts (Jeles's numbers — 0.5.1, 99 commits, 8 tags, the withdrawn `jeles>=0.5.1,<0.6.0` cap, the SSRF-patch example — describe Jeles's history, not Forge's, and belong in Jeles's own config). release-type 'simple' maintains CHANGELOG.md and the tag and edits no version file — correct here because hatch-vcs derives the version from the tag, so there is no second copy to keep in step. bump-minor-pre-major is FALSE with bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major false, so below 1.0: feat -> minor, fix and everything unlabelled -> patch, and a breaking change -> 1.0.0. UNLIKE JELES, bump-minor-pre-major has been false here since this file was first committed to this repo — there was never a 'used to be true, then changed' moment for Forge to narrate, so this comment does not repeat Jeles's WHY IT CHANGED story. As of 2026-09-12: 70 commits and 9 tags (v0.1.0 through v0.7.2) in this repository's history, and zero commits in the full log carry `!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer (checked, not assumed) — this package has never had a breaking change either, so the 1.0.0 trigger is exactly as untested here as it was in Jeles's original telling. The consequence is not hypothetical, though: willow-mcp pins `forge-play>=0.1.0,<1.0.0` (its pyproject.toml) on the strength of this exact setting, because bump-minor-pre-major false is what makes a breaking change here guaranteed to leave 0.x rather than land inside the cap unnoticed. WHAT STILL IS NOT GUARANTEED: this keys off the commit type, so it only holds when a breaking change is actually written `feat!:`/`fix!:`/etc. or carries a BREAKING CHANGE footer — a break mislabelled `refactor:` still ships as a patch, and willow-mcp's cap would not catch it. See willow-mcp's docs/design/fleet-versioning.md Rule 1 for the general argument; its tests/test_fleet_versioning.py is a contract test against the really-installed package, and Forge does not yet have an equivalent test of its own.
$comment-sections: Section names mirror Keep a Changelog, which willow-mcp's CHANGELOG already follows. Commit types outside this list (the fleet also uses hooks:, gate:, skills:, server:, envelopes:) are ignored for both the changelog and the version bump.
$comment-what-cuts-a-release: EVERY type listed above without "hidden": true cuts a release on its own — not just feat and fix. This comment previously claimed otherwise, and it was wrong: v0.4.1 was tagged and published to PyPI for a single ci: commit that changed a workflow file and nothing a user installs. That was survivable while releases were merged by hand, because you saw what was in them; release-please.yml now arms auto-merge, so an un-hidden type ships to PyPI unattended, and a PyPI version can never be reused.
$comment-hidden-rule: The line is: does this commit change what someone gets from `pip install forge-play`? docs/test/ci do not — tests and workflows are not packaged, and a README edit only moves the PyPI page — so they are hidden and ride along with the next real release. build and deps stay visible because a dependency or packaging change genuinely alters the installed artifact, and hiding them would mean a dependency fix never reaching anyone, silently. refactor and perf stay visible because they change shipped code, and a version number is what you point at when a refactor turns out to have broken something. Hidden also means absent from CHANGELOG.md — release-please has no 'list it but do not release on it' setting, so this is a real trade, taken deliberately.
